guide.summary: Each caller's own mailbox: Gmail search syntax, capped bodies, reply threading, drafts that never send.
guide.content:
# Gmail usage (draft-only)

Acts as the signed-in person's own Gmail through Workspace delegation: read mail and write drafts, never send.

Connection purpose: Staff email for alice

## Whose mailbox

Every call reads and writes the mailbox deployment config maps the caller
to; an agent acts as the owner of the pool it came through, unless the deployment fixes one shared mailbox that every caller, agent or person, acts as. No argument
names a mailbox. A call with none mapped fails `auth_required`; only an operator can change
that.

## Reading

- `search_threads` takes Gmail search syntax; reuse the person's own
  phrasing (`from:`, `subject:`, `newer_than:7d`, `is:unread`,
  `label:`). Page with `page.nextCursor` and the same query.
- `get_thread` returns messages oldest first with bodies capped by
  `maxBodyChars`; a cut body ends with a truncation marker. A long thread
  pages: follow `page.nextCursor` until `hasMore` is false, with the same
  arguments. `conflict` means the thread changed under the cursor; read it
  again from the start. Reduce inside
  `execute_code` before returning a long thread.
- Results default to at most 192 KiB; `list_labels` pages the same way.
- `get_message` and `get_thread` list attachment metadata. An attached or
  forwarded email is an attachment, not the body.
- `bodyFormat: "unavailable"` means Gmail stored the body apart from the
  message and it is too large to read here; say so rather than summarizing.
- `get_message`, each `get_thread` message, and `get_draft` return `bodyNote`
  when decoding falls back to UTF-8 for an unsupported charset. The note
  survives character and result-byte truncation, including `maxBodyChars: 0`
  when inline body data is decoded. It counts toward the result's byte limit.

## Attachments

- `get_attachment` takes `messageId` and the listing's immutable `partId`.
  Prefer `partId`, which stays stable across message reads, including an
  empty id for a root attachment. `attachmentId` is an alternative that
  Gmail can rotate between reads. When both are supplied, `partId` wins and
  the fresh message's download id is used. Read the listing again after
  an unknown-id refusal; never store an attachmentId for later use.
- Small attachments can have inline data and no attachmentId. Use their
  partId too. Only carried attachment parts can be read, never arbitrary
  message body parts or blind download ids.
- Text, JSON, XML, calendar invites, CSV, and `message/rfc822` return
  `format: "text"` and `content` decoded in the declared charset. An unsupported
  charset produces an explicit `note` that decoding used UTF-8. Message bodies
  return the notice separately as `bodyNote`.
  Parsed forwarded emails render From, To, Date, Subject, and their own
  plain body, else HTML converted to text. Raw forwarded data is preferred
  when present. A forwarded email without readable text returns an
  `unavailable` note.
  `maxChars` defaults to 12,000 code points, at most 100,000. A character
  or byte cut ends with a truncation marker and `contentTruncated: true`.
  Reduce attachment text inside `execute_code` before returning it.
- Binary attachments return `format: "base64"` and standard base64 in
  `content`. Pass it unchanged to Drive `create_file` as `contentBase64`,
  with `name: filename` and `mimeType`. File creation is a write: use
  `call_destructive_tool` or a program on a writable endpoint for that step.
- Downloads, text and binary, are limited to 1 MiB. Declared size is
  checked before a separate download. Parsed forwarded emails check the sum
  of descendant sizes before downloading any stored body, and return that
  sum as `size`. Attachment data must match both the message part's declared
  size and the download response's size when supplied; inconsistent payloads
  fail rather than return incomplete files. Binary content must also fit the
  whole-result `maxBytes`, which defaults to 192 KiB. `format: "unavailable"`
  returns a note and no content when it cannot fit. Raising `maxChars`
  or `maxBytes` cannot bypass the download cap.
- Raise `maxBytes` only for a direct `call_tool` read, from 64 KiB up to
  4 MiB, as with Drive `get_file_content`. `execute_code` cannot receive
  large results; keep the default there. Direct-call results may be paged.

## Drafting

- `create_draft` saves a draft and never sends it; tell the person it is
  waiting in Drafts. There is no send, delete, or label tool.
- To reply, pass `replyToMessageId`: the draft joins that thread with
  In-Reply-To and References set, and subject (Re: …) and `to` default
  from that message's Reply-To, else its From. Keep the Re: subject or Gmail
  may start a new thread.
- `update_draft` replaces the body entirely; send the full new text.
  From, To, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To, Subject, the thread, and reply headers are
  kept unless restated; no other header is. A draft with attachments or
  inline images is refused, unchanged — Gmail's update would delete them.
- Gmail sets From to the mailbox itself; there is no From argument.

tools.name: search_threads
tools.description: Search the user's Gmail threads with Gmail query syntax, newest first, returning subject, senders, date, and snippet per thread. Bodies need get_thread.

query.description: Gmail search syntax, as in the Gmail search box: from:, to:, subject:, label:, is:unread, has:attachment, newer_than:7d, in:inbox. Omit for everything.

includeSpamTrash.description: Include Spam and Trash, which Gmail leaves out by default.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1 to 25; defaults to 10. Connecta's cap, below Gmail's 500, because each row costs a metadata read.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the previous page of this same call; another call's cursor is refused. Pass it back unchanged.

tools.name: get_thread
tools.description: Get a Gmail thread's messages, oldest first, with headers, plain-text bodies capped by maxBodyChars, and attachment metadata. Read attachments with get_attachment using partId. A long thread pages by cursor.

threadId.description: Thread id from search_threads or a message's threadId.

maxBodyChars.description: Characters of body text kept per message, 0 to 100000; defaults to 3000. Longer bodies end with a truncation marker, as does any body past connecta's 192 KiB result limit.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from this thread's previous page, same maxBodyChars. A page ends before 192 KiB; a thread changed before that point answers conflict.

bodyNote.description: Decoding notice, preserved when the body is truncated.

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Get one Gmail message with headers, its plain-text body (HTML converted only when no text part exists), and attachment metadata. Read attachments with get_attachment using partId.

messageId.description: Message id from get_thread, or a draft's messageId.

maxBodyChars.description: Characters of body text kept per message, 0 to 100000; defaults to 12000. Longer bodies end with a truncation marker, as does any body past connecta's 192 KiB result limit.

raw.description: Return Gmail's untouched message resource (every header, base64url part bodies) instead of the projection. Refused past connecta's 192 KiB result limit.

bodyNote.description: Decoding notice, preserved when the body is truncated.

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: Read a Gmail attachment by immutable partId: text with its charset, or small binaries as standard base64 for Drive create_file. Refuses oversized downloads; text is capped by maxChars and the whole result by maxBytes.

messageId.description: Message id from get_message, get_thread, or get_draft.

partId.description: Immutable partId from the attachment listing, including an empty root id. Preferred; authoritative when attachmentId is also supplied.

attachmentId.description: Alternative attachmentId from the listing. Gmail can rotate it between reads; prefer partId.

maxChars.description: Text code points kept; defaults to 12000. Longer text ends with a truncation marker. Ignored for binaries.

maxBytes.description: Whole-result UTF-8 JSON byte budget; defaults to 196608. Raise it only for a direct call_tool; execute_code cannot receive large results.

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description: List the user's Gmail labels, system and user-created, with the ids messages carry; no message counts. Search by name with label: in search_threads.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the previous page. Gmail returns every label at once; connecta pages them so thousands still fit, and answers conflict if the list changed.

tools.name: list_drafts
tools.description: List the user's Gmail drafts, newest first, with subject, recipients, and snippet. Use get_draft for a body.

query.description: Gmail search syntax, as in the Gmail search box: from:, to:, subject:, label:, is:unread, has:attachment, newer_than:7d, in:inbox. Omit for everything.

limit.description: Rows per page, 1 to 25; defaults to 10. Connecta's cap, below Gmail's 500, because each row costs a metadata read.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor from the previous page of this same call; another call's cursor is refused. Pass it back unchanged.

tools.name: get_draft
tools.description: Get one Gmail draft's headers and plain-text body by draft id. Reading it never sends it.

draftId.description: Draft id from list_drafts or create_draft.

maxBodyChars.description: Characters of body text kept per message, 0 to 100000; defaults to 12000. Longer bodies end with a truncation marker, as does any body past connecta's 192 KiB result limit.

bodyNote.description: Decoding notice, preserved when the body is truncated.

tools.name: create_draft
tools.description: Create a Gmail draft, optionally as a reply in an existing thread. It is saved, never sent: the user reviews and sends it in Gmail.

subject.description: Subject line; any language. A reply defaults to Re: and the original subject, which Gmail needs to keep it in the thread.

body.description: Plain-text body. Always required; it is what clients without HTML show.

htmlBody.description: Optional HTML alternative to body, sent beside it. Omit for a plain-text draft.

replyToMessageId.description: Message id (from get_thread or get_message) this draft replies to: sets its thread, In-Reply-To, and References, and defaults subject and to from it.

tools.name: update_draft
tools.description: Replace a Gmail draft's body, keeping its sender, recipients, subject, Reply-To, and thread unless restated. Refuses a draft with attachments. Never sends it.

draftId.description: Draft id from list_drafts or create_draft.

to.description: To; omit to keep the current recipients.

cc.description: Cc; omit to keep the current recipients.

bcc.description: Bcc; omit to keep the current recipients.

subject.description: Subject line; omit to keep the current one.

body.description: The new plain-text body, replacing the old one entirely.

htmlBody.description: Optional HTML alternative; omitting it drops any HTML the draft had.

replyToMessageId.description: Message id (from get_thread or get_message) this draft replies to: sets its thread, In-Reply-To, and References, and defaults subject and to from it.
